ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory under Article 9-12 of AML Law 2022 and Circular 10/2023/TT-NHNN: risk-based Customer Due Diligence (CDD) and Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) for all designated non-financial professions, including securities brokerage (ISIC 6611); mandatory identification of domestic/foreign PEPs, immediate family and close associates; automated screening of clients, UBOs and beneficial owners against (i) UNSC Resolution 1267/1373/2253/2259 consolidated lists implemented through Viet Nam's Single National List (Ministry of Public Security roadmap), (ii) OFAC SDN list as a condition of USD correspondent wire rails and Visa/Mastercard payments, and (iii) the State Bank of Viet Nam's domestic terrorist-financing and ML-convicted list; ongoing transaction monitoring with 30-day periodic re-screening and immediate freezing of tainted assets under Ordinance on Asset Freezing No. 28/2013/UBTVQH13 and governmental Decree No. 44/2014/ND-CP.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Business Registration Portal of Viet Nam (Cổng thông tin quốc gia về đăng ký doanh nghiệp) — https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn; over-the-counter filing at the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) one-stop-shop of the intended province (HCMC or Hanoi).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The legally operative enterprise name must be in the Vietnamese script (Tiếng Việt, Latin alphabet with Vietnamese diacritics). Per Enterprise Law 2020 Art. 38 and Decree 01/2021/ND-CP Art. 33, a Vietnamese-trader name may include foreign-credit letters F, J, W, Z only in loanwords/derived proper nouns; for foreign-invested LLCs, the registered Vietnamese name governs all filings with DPI, SSC and SBV. A concurrent English/Latin transliteration may be registered as an alternative denomination (tên phụ, 'secondary name') placed after the Vietnamese name, but all statutory documents are prepared in Tiếng Việt and foreign-sourced documentation is apostilled/legalized and attached with certified Vietnamese translation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: State authority names of Viet Nam: 'Chính phủ', 'Quốc hội', 'Bộ Công an', 'Tòa án', 'Viện kiểm sát', 'Quân đội', 'Công an nhân dân' (heavier administrative prohibition under Decree 01/2021 Art. 38(2))
Historical / cultural symbols and improper national heroes or revolutionary units not authorized by the competent ministry
Words violating national sovereignty or public interest (territorial claims, ethnic discrimination, obscene lexemes) — absolute prohibition under Enterprise Law Art. 38(3)
Regulated financial intermediation token: 'Chứng khoán' (securities) and 'Sàn giao dịch chứng khoán' (securities trading floor) — prior non-objection of the State Securities Commission (SSC) required
Banking token: 'Ngân hàng' (bank) — prior approval of the State Bank of Viet Nam (SBV) required
Insurance token: 'Bảo hiểm' (insurance) — prior approval of the Ministry of Finance required

Other license-gated industry tokens: 'Hàng không' (airline), 'Hạt nhân' (nuclear), 'Vũ khí' (weaponry), 'Thăm dò' (exploration), 'Khoáng sản' (mineral extraction) — prior ministerial or provincial licensing consent required

Misleading commercial token: 'Offshore', 'Offshore Financial Centre', 'Nước ngoài' when used to misrepresent the regulated Viet Nam-incorporated status of a brokerage performing cross-border services — considered misleading to stakeholders under Enterprise Law Art. 38(3)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name rejection is processed through the National Business Registration Portal as a negative administrative determination. Stage 1 Remedial Track: (i) Informal Cure — amend the proposed name and resubmit the pre-incorporation dossier forthwith; no separate state fee is charged for a new name search. (ii) Formal Administrative Complaint — under Decree 01/2021/ND-CP and Law on Complaints No. 02/2011/QH13, file a written complaint with the Director-General of the provincial DPI within 90 days of the refusal, attaching legal argument that the name is not identical/confusingly similar to a registered name. (iii) Higher Appeal — if the DPI upholds refusal, appeal to the provincial People's Committee; exhaustion of administrative remedies opens judicial review before the Administrative Court under Law on Administrative Proceedings No. 93/2015/QH13. (iv) Ministerial Name Coordination — for tokens such as 'Chứng khoán', the applicant must simultaneously seek a preliminary no-objection letter from the SSC; the DPI cannot clear the name until SSC consent is placed on file. Pending any appeal and SSC coordination, the 30-day name-reservation window runs; the applicant may re-tender the reservation after each substantive amendment on payment of the standard registration fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual/rent-a-desk (mailbox-only) offices are not acceptable as the statutory registered address for an SSC-licensed securities brokerage. Decree 01/2021/ND-CP Art. 25 requires the registered address to be a real, usable place where records and corporate seal are satisfactorily retained; Law on Securities 2019 and Decree 128/2021/ND-CP impose a physical head-office and operational facility in Viet Nam (segregated client-asset administration, trading room, BCP systems) before the securities license is granted. Stage 1 may use a serviced office address as the eventual operational HQ, but it must be a true fixed-premises lease — and a vendor cannot market a 'virtual offshore' address in Viet Nam for this license class.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High — quantified at approximately 85-90% within the first 12 months of license issuance: the State Securities Commission performs mandatory pre-license site inspections under its administrative inspection power in the Law on Securities, and the State Bank of Viet Nam's AML/CFT supervisory unit may announce or conduct unannounced physical examinations under Article 47 of AML Law 2022. For ISIC 6611 high-risk special-license brokerage, the assumption in the compliance program is a site audit in the first year; dedicated server/record location, separate client-money bank accounts and physical board-meeting minutes must be presentable on-site.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (GDT) of the Ministry of Finance, Socialist Republic of Viet Nam. Electronic filing and registration portal: etax.gdt.gov.vn; national electronic invoice database: hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn; export/customs electronic declaration system: edx.customs.gov.vn. Provincial-level tax departments (provincial Tax Departments) administer the local taxpayer files, acceptance of registrations, and field audits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A 100% foreign-invested LLC must first obtain an Investment Registration Certificate (IRC) and an Enterprise Registration Certificate (ERC), issued by the provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) or the authorized industrial/export-processing zone authority. Tax registration is integrated with enterprise registration: after ERC issuance, the national business registration database transmits the data to the GDT, which automatically issues a 13-digit tax identification number (TIN) (official name in Vietnamese: Ma so thue) within 3 working days. The TIN is simultaneously the VAT identification number for the LLC. If automatic issuance is not completed, the taxpayer files tax registration form 01-DK-TCT with the managing provincial tax office. For a securities brokerage, the State Securities Commission of Vietnam must additionally issue the securities business license under the Securities Law 54/2019/QH14 before operational services commence; TIN issuance nonetheless begins from the ERC date such that corporate income tax and VAT filing obligations accrue.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: a Vietnamese LLC is a resident taxpayer subject to corporate income tax (CIT) at the standard rate of 20% on worldwide income. There is no pass-through or partnership tax-transparent regime at federal/equivalent level; profits are taxed at the LLC level and dividends distributed to the foreign shareholder are not subject to additional dividend withholding tax in Viet Nam. The LLC is not located in a Tax_Exempt_Zone by default, but may qualify for CIT incentives (10% or 15% rates) if operating in eligible high-tech, software, or large-scale investment sectors and if licensed as an export-processing enterprise respectively.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Viet Nam does not grant any check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch entity election; the LLC's entity-level tax classification is statutory, not elective. Available tax elections and administrative mechanisms include: (i) applying for preferential CIT rates (10%, 15% or 20%) under new-investment and high-tech incentive criteria; (ii) electing simplified VAT declaration or submission of consolidated invoice data under the electronic invoice regime; (iii) applying for an advance pricing arrangement (APA) under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP for transfer pricing stabilization; (iv) electing the export-processing enterprise (EPE) status which carries VAT and customs duty privileges; and (v) choosing to be treated as a small and medium enterprise for reduced administrative formalities. No election can convert the LLC into a pass-through vehicle for Vietnamese tax purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (value added tax; official Vietnamese name: Thue gia tri gia tang)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VND 1,000,000,000 (one billion Vietnamese dong) of annual revenue for mandatory VAT registration by business households and individuals; an LLC is always required to register for and declare VAT without regard to turnover because VAT registration is mandatory upon enterprise registration. Securities brokerage services are statutory VAT-exempt supplies, so the offshore securities brokerage will not charge output VAT at the 10% rate and is generally not entitled to reclaim input VAT attributable to exempt supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory nationwide e-invoicing has applied since 1 July 2022 under Decree 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC. Every LLC must issue e-invoices in standardized XML format, affix a qualified electronic signature, and transmit invoice data to the national electronic invoice portal (hoadondientu.gdt.gov.vn) through certified e-invoice service providers. The GDT performs automated business-rule validation, QR-code/2D-code generation, digital stamping, and risk-based real-time fiscal clearance for high-risk refund claimants. E-invoices without a tax authority code are permitted only after successful registration of the invoice form with the tax authority; all export zero-rated or VAT-exempt services must nevertheless be documented on compliant e-invoices matching the customs and banking records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Law on VAT and Circular 219/2013/TT-BTC (Article 9), the 0% VAT rate applies to goods physically exported from Viet Nam or sold into non-tariff zones (export-processing zones, bonded warehouses) and to services supplied to foreign organizations/individuals where the services are consumed entirely outside Viet Nam, including international transport. Eligibility requires a documentary chain evidencing the export, delivery abroad, and payment received from abroad in convertible foreign currency. However, Vietnamese securities business services, including equities brokerage, derivatives brokerage, and related security intermediary services, are statutory VAT-exempt items under Article 5(4) of the Law on VAT and therefore cannot receive 0% VAT treatment; the offshore securities brokerage's commission income is VAT-exempt, not zero-rated, and input VAT attributable to these exempt supplies is blocked. Ancillary non-exempt services (for example market data licensing or bespoke cross-border research) may be eligible for 0% if the contract, offshore consumption, and inbound payment documentation meet all conditions.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
Export sales contract, commercial invoice, and packing list
Bank SWIFT credit advice or bank statement showing receipt of convertible foreign currency in the LLC's Vietnamese account

For offshore services: cross-border service agreement, compliant e-invoice, evidence of offshore consumption (client acceptance or service completion certificate), and banking proof of payment from the foreign client
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Viet Nam applies risk-based VAT refund screening by the GDT; export zero-rating and refund claims are priority audit targets, particularly for high-risk financial-sector taxpayers. Failure to satisfy the substantive and documentation conditions exposes the LLC to reversal of the 0% rate and imposition of output VAT at 10%, disallowance of input VAT credits, reassessment of refunded amounts with late-payment interest at 0.02% per day, and administrative fines under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP ranging from 10% to 100% of the underdeclared tax. Fraudulent refund claims, false e-invoicing, or fabricated export documentation may constitute tax evasion under Penal Code 2015 Article 200 and invoicing fraud under Article 202, carrying substantial fines, imprisonment, and confiscation of assets; systemic violations additionally expose the licensed brokerage to State Securities Commission sanctions including license suspension or revocation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Viet Nam maintains a managed convertibility regime. The Vietnamese Dong (VND) is not freely convertible offshore. Current account transactions are substantially convertible through SBV-licensed authorized banks, while capital account transactions, including foreign direct investment equity contributions, shareholder loans, and profit remittances, are generally subject to registration, licensing, or post-verification by the SBV and the relevant ministry. For the VN_LLC offshore securities brokerage, inbound management fees, brokerage commissions, and client settlements are treated as service exports or current account receipts, but every receipt must be repatriated into a licensed foreign currency account at an SBV-authorized bank before any further disposition. Dividend and profit remittance is permitted only after annually audited financial statements, corporate income tax finalization, and full satisfaction of all statutory tax and social obligations. The entity must maintain a valid Investment Registration Certificate and Enterprise Registration Certificate reflecting the securities brokerage activity, and, if it creates a local presence for retail investors, a licence from the Ministry of Finance/State Securities Commission under the Law on Securities; without such a licence, the entity may only conduct cross-border brokerage that does not solicit Vietnamese retail investors through prohibited distribution channels.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under Circular 15/2015/TT-NHNN and the Ordinance on Foreign Exchange, export proceeds arising from goods and services must be repatriated to a foreign currency account at an SBV-authorized licensed bank within 180 days from the date of completing customs clearance for goods, or from the date the service is performed and invoiced for services. There is no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts; the entity may retain 100% of qualifying export proceeds in a foreign currency account. Conversion into VND is made voluntarily at the authorized bank's published buying rate when the entity needs VND liquidity. For the offshore securities brokerage, the entire fee, commission, rebate, or other service consideration must be credited to a local foreign currency account within the statutory 180-day window; no netting or offshore retention is permitted unless the transaction qualifies for an exemption issued by the SBV.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a standalone banking or client-money holding solution. Offshore digital EMI platforms and virtual banking-as-a-service providers (e.g., Wise Business, Revolut Business, or similar unlicensed EMIs) are not SBV-licensed credit institutions and cannot lawfully hold client funds, issue VND IBANs, or participate in Vietnamese domestic clearing. Their viable role is limited to: (i) an offshore multicurrency receiving or settlement application-layer for non-VND transactions; or (ii) a technology/API middleware that connects the licensed local bank to the brokerage's trade platform. All domestic VND flows, sa, and segregated client money movements must be executed through an SBV-authorized bank. An unlicensed EMI may never be used as a liquidity mirror, an escrow holder for retail clients, or a substitute for a securities company's segregated client account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is effectively mandatory for the offshore-owned high-risk securities brokerage. Tier-1 Vietnamese banks require the legal representative and the ultimate beneficial owner, or their duly authorized signatory under a notarized power of attorney, to attend an in-person KYC/AML interview at the branch before account activation. Remote-only account opening is not available in practice for ISIC 6611 high-risk license entities. Documents executed outside Viet Nam must be notarized, translated into Vietnamese, and consular legalized because Viet Nam has not acceded to the Apostille Convention. At a minimum, the bank will require the legal representative to present original passports, board resolutions, audited entity financial statements, AML/CFT policy, and evidence of the securities brokerage licence or a regulatory explanation of the offshore exemption.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk industry classification: ISIC 6611 retail agency for equities, CFDs and derivative instruments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory securities business licence issued by the State Securities Commission of Viet Nam, or a written legal opinion confirming the offshore brokerage exemption; board-approved AML/CFT compliance manual; business model narrative; transaction monitoring system specification; independent audit report on internal controls; professional indemnity insurance certificate; sanctions screening policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBOs or multi-layer offshore ownership with no local economic substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO chain org chart certified by legal counsel; beneficial ownership declarations; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence; audited consolidated financial statements of the ultimate parent; bank reference letters from the parent's reputable first-tier bank; Vietnamese tax identification numbers; proof of registered local address and substance such as contracts, invoices, payroll records, and office lease.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border wire transfers to high-risk cities, unlicensed brokers, or opaque counterparties involved in leveraged derivative settlement
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Counterparty AML/KYC files; sanctions and adverse-media screening logs; jurisdiction risk matrix; geo-blocking logs demonstrating prohibition of FATF high-risk jurisdictions; SWIFT purpose codes that match the commercial rationale; daily reconciliation of segregated client funds; executed master agreements with licensed prime brokers or counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Retail client deposits through card rails (Visa/Mastercard) with potential money laundering or chargeback abuse
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Segregated client ledger showing investor-level deposit and withdrawal matching; source-of-funds declarations per client; card processor merchant agreement and licencing; T+1 or faster reconciliation to the segregated account; chargeback monitoring and refund procedures; automated suspicious transaction reporting; external audit trail retention complying with Decree 116/2023/ND-CP on AML implementation.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Foreign direct investment equity or subordinated capital must be subscribed under the Investment Registration Certificate and Enterprise Registration Certificate and wired by SWIFT MT103 into the bank's dedicated FDI Capital Escrow Account. The remitter must use the SBV-prescribed transaction purpose code for direct investment capital contribution and include the IRC or ERC reference number in the SWIFT field 70 remittance information. The receiving bank validates that the contribution is made within the statutory capital contribution period of 90 days unless extended, records the capital inflow on the SBV monitoring system, and issues a receipt confirming the foreign currency converted into VND if required. Offshore shareholder loans over VND 1 million or equivalent must be registered with the SBV as an enterprise foreign borrowing prior to inflow; loans that are unregistered may not be remitted or may be converted into equity only after SBV enforcement action.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements and operational disbursements must be executed through SWIFT-cleared rails. For routine cross-border fees, commissions, rebates, and trade settlements involving the offshore brokerage, use SWIFT MT103 for single client-facing transactions and MT202COV for interbank cover payments when the beneficiary account is held at a different institution. Any settlement related to equities, CFDs, or exchange-traded instruments should use a corresponding trade reference code and be matched against the prime broker or execution venue's contract notes. Commercial letters of credit are not applicable to the core brokerage activity except where physically settled commodities or documentary trade underlyings are part of a licensed derivatives portfolio; for such goods-based trades, Issuing Bank LCs under UCP600 are permitted. Domestic VND clearing may be routed through NAPAS instant or batch clearing only for local operating expenses; all client money disbursements to overseas retail clients must use SWIFT MT103 and be covered by the segregated client account ledger. Card funding via Visa/Mastercard is permissible only through an SBV-licensed merchant acquirer, with card-settlement proceeds swept into the segregated client account no later than the next business day and then onward transmitted by wire rails under the brokerage's treasury policy.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX forwards with SBV-licensed authorized banks on documented underlying current-account exposure, including service fee receipts and future dividend/profit remittances, pursuant to Circular 15/2015/TT-NHNN and Circular 26/2018/TT-NHNN.
FX swaps (spot against forward) with licensed local credit institutions for temporary VND/USD liquidity management and repricing of operational cash flows.

Cross-currency swaps or cross-currency interest-rate swaps with licensed banks for long-term foreign-currency borrowings, provided the underlying borrowings are registered with the SBV and the hedge does not create an uncovered speculative position.

FX options purchased from SBV-licensed credit institutions, including call or put options, when used to hedge a defined and documented economic exposure arising from actual or anticipated current account or capital account transactions.

Combination hedging structures such as collars and ratio forwards, but only where the licensed local bank documents the underlying exposure and the hedge tenor does not exceed the underlying transaction liquidity cycle.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 calendar days after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities, no later than 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of VND 10–20 million (approx. USD 390–780); continued non-filing for two consecutive years after written reminder may lead to revocation of the Enterprise Registration Certificate under Decree 01/2021/ND-CP.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Finalization Return (Quyết toán thuế TNDN)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Department / General Department of Taxation via e-tax portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 calendar days after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities, no later than 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine up to VND 25 million (approx. USD 980); late-payment interest of 0.03% per day; escalated penalties under Tax Administration Law 38/2019/QH14.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Audited Financial Statements (Báo cáo tài chính đã kiểm toán)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Department and State Securities Commission of Vietnam
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 calendar days after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities, no later than 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties under Securities Law 2019 and Accounting Law 2015; securities license suspension or revocation for failure to submit audited financial statements; tax authorities may impose penalties up to VND 50 million (approx. USD 1,960).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Investment Report (Báo cáo đầu tư)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Registration Agency / Provincial Department of Planning and Investment / Export Processing Zone Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 calendar days after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities, no later than 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine under Decree 122/2021/ND-CP from VND 5–15 million (approx. USD 195–585); repeated failure may result in suspension of investment incentives and administrative revocation procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business License Tax (Lệ phí môn bài)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable annually no later than 30 January; newly established entities pay within 30 days from issuance of Enterprise Registration Certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest of 0.03% per day and administrative fine of 0.5–3 times the overdue amount; compulsory collection and enterprise registration enforcement after repeated non-payment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Compliance and Financial Condition Report to State Securities Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 calendar days after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities, no later than 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: License suspension or withdrawal; administrative fine up to VND 150 million (approx. USD 5,880) under Securities Law 54/2019/QH14; mandatory remediation plan and reporting.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for all foreign-invested economic organizations irrespective of revenue size under Accounting Law 2015 and Decree 17/2012/ND-CP; also mandatory for all licensed securities companies under Securities Law 2019 and Circular 99/2014/TT-BTC.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnamese Accounting Standards (VAS) for statutory annual financial statements; IFRS as adopted in Vietnam permitted as supplementary or consolidated reporting under Circular 202/2014/TT-BTC.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No separate UBO annual confirmation form exists. The LLC must maintain an internal Register of Members, update it within 10 days of any transfer, and report changes to the DPI within 10 days. The annual enterprise report reconfirms the member/UBO list as at the fiscal year-end. Under the Anti-Money Laundering Law 19/2023/QH15, the securities broker must also maintain customer beneficial-ownership due diligence records and risk-rate such clients annually.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Sổ đăng ký thành viên)
Register of Charter Capital Contributions (Sổ đăng ký góp vốn)
Minute Book and Resolutions of Members' Council (Sổ biên bản họp và quyết định của Hội đồng thành viên)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Statutory tax holidays and preferential deductions are available under the Law on Corporate Income Tax No. 14/2008/QH12 as amended. Preferential rates may include 10% for 15 years for high-tech enterprises, software production, and certain encouraged sectors; a 20% rate for the first 2 years and 15% for the next 4 years for eligible new projects in industrial parks and economic zones; and reduced rates for small- and medium-sized enterprises under the Law on Support for SMEs. Additional deductions include a 5-year carryforward period for tax losses, and research and development expenditure incentives under certain conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 02/TNDN (Annual CIT Finalization Return), filed electronically via the Vietnamese General Department of Taxation (GDT) online portal (https://thuedientu.gdt.gov.vn). Taxpayers must use the e-tax portal for filing; accompanying schedules include Form 01/QTT-TNDN and transfer pricing schedules if applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (with quarterly provisional payments and annual finalization declaration)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual finalization return must be filed within 90 days after the end of the fiscal year (for calendar-year taxpayers: by March 31 of the following year). Quarterly provisional tax payments are due no later than the 30th day of the first month of the next quarter. Taxpayers with derivative or unconventional fiscal years must follow the fiscal year approved by tax authorities and submit returns within 90 days of the fiscal year end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - General Information: Tax identification number, company name, address, fiscal year, tax period
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Identify the taxpayer and the reporting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a foreign-invested LLC, enter the Vietnamese tax code and corporate name exactly as per the Enterprise Registration Certificate. Non-resident shareholders are not separately identified to this form unless the company acts as a withholding agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1 - Revenue: Total gross revenue from business activities
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all revenue from securities brokerage commissions, margin interest, custodial fees, and other services rendered after excluding VAT-inclusive items as appropriate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue from offshore clients may be partially sourced outside Vietnam if the brokerage service is rendered offshore and the transaction occurs on a foreign exchange. For the Vietnamese LLC, report only revenue attributable to the Vietnamese operation and maintain documentary source evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 2 - Deductible Expenses: Total expenses attributable to revenue generation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Include salaries, commissions paid to introducing brokers, clearing and settlement fees, software, rent, and administrative overhead; comply with the actual-expense principle under Circular 96/2015/TT-BTC and expense documentation requirements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border payments to offshore affiliates are deductible only if supported by valid contracts, VAT invoice/withholding documentation, and if the transfer pricing arm’s length conditions are met. Expenses without proper Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) withholding are non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 3 - Tax-exempt income: Income exempt under Article 4 of the Law on CIT
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report income exempt from CIT, if any. For securities brokerage, generally only non-business incidental income may qualify; investment income from government bonds or certain project income might qualify under legal provisions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned entities cannot automatically exempt income without explicit domestic or treaty basis. Exemptions require prior approval and are narrowly construed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 4 - Loss carryforward: Amount of prior-year losses carried forward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Use remaining losses from the last 5 years. Losses must be offset against taxable income in chronological order.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The loss offset for the Vietnamese LLC is available for Vietnamese-source business income only. Foreign losses are not deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 5 - Taxable income: Income net of exempt income and loss carryforwards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as gross revenue minus deductible expenses minus tax-exempt income plus other taxable income, then reduced by loss carryforwards.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attributable to Vietnamese operations. Apportionment between Vietnamese and non-Vietnamese source income is allowed only if the taxpayer maintains clear and separate accounting.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 6 - CIT rate: Applicable tax rate
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Standard rate is 20%. Preferential rates (10%, 15%, 17%) apply only with a valid investment incentive certificate for eligible sectors/regions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-invested securities brokerage entities do not normally qualify for sector-based incentives unless located in an approved IT/economic zone. The offshore brokerage activity itself is not a favored category. Rates must match the approved license and certificate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 7 - CIT payable: Provisional tax paid and additional amount due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate tax payable based on taxable income. If provisional quarterly payments are less than the actual annual tax, the difference must be paid with the final return; underpayment for the year may trigger late interest if each quarter underpaid by more than 20%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No treaty rate applies to corporate income tax direct computation for a PE/LLC. The LLC is taxed at the standard rate regardless of the residence of shareholders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 8 - Related-party transaction declaration (Schedule, Giao dịch liên kết)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Complete the transfer pricing declaration forms (Form 01/QL-GTTT under Circular 132/2020/ND-CP) disclosing transactions with related parties, values, methods, and basis for arm's length pricing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must include all transactions with offshore headquarters, affiliated brokers, allocating shareholders, IP owners, and lenders. All cross-border related-party financial transactions are subject to transfer pricing obligations and documentation defence requirements.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual finalization return attracts a fine under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP: VND 2 million to VND 5 million for filing between the deadline and 1 day late; VND 5–10 million for 1–10 days late; VND 15–25 million for 10–30 days late; VND 30–50 million for 1–3 months late; VND 50–75 million for exceeding 3 months or if the return contains incomplete information. Additionally, late payment interest at 0.03% per day is charged on any CIT underpaid or remaining payable. Non-filing allows the tax authority to issue an official tax assessment notice based on available information.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% (Vietnam does not impose a separate dividend withholding tax on distributions made by a foreign-invested LLC to its corporate shareholders. Dividends are paid from after-tax profits and are not subject to additional CIT withholding. However, dividends paid to individuals are subject to personal income tax at 5% under the domestic law if the recipient is a resident individual. For non-resident corporate shareholders, no additional dividend withholding tax is imposed under the Law on CIT. Treaty relief is generally irrelevant for corporate shareholders due to the zero rate.).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain treaty protection for income streams that do attract Vietnamese source taxation (e.g., interest, royalties, technical service fees, or business profits attributable to a permanent establishment), the beneficial owner must submit a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty jurisdiction tax authority to the Vietnamese paying entity or withholding agent before the payment date. The Vietnamese LLC must retain the TRC, a statement of treaty entitlement, and supporting breakdown of income. The payment is then made under the reduced treaty withholding rate. If the full domestic rate was withheld, a refund application must be filed with the General Department of Taxation (GDT) within the limitation period (normally 10 years), with accompanying TRC, contracts, invoices, and foreign tax credit details. The LLC must use the approved forms under Circular 156/2013/TT-BTC and subsequent guidance. Vietnam’s double tax treaties generally follow the OECD/UN Model, with beneficial ownership and limitation-of-benefits provisions in many modern treaties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding (Foreign Contractor Tax - FCT) is imposed as a combined withholding tax comprising CIT and VAT for payments to non-residents. For royalties: deemed CIT rate is 10% on gross royalty income, plus deemed VAT rate of 5%, resulting in total 15% when the foreign supplier does not implement a Vietnamese permanent establishment. Treaty rates for royalties are commonly 10% (or 5% under some agreements if the IP relates to equipment), and the VAT component may still apply but often is exempt for pure license when no service is rendered in Vietnam. For interest: statutory rate for FCT on interest is 5% CIT (deemed) and 0% VAT; treaty rate for interest is typically 10% (or 5% under certain treaties). Therefore, the standard domestic withholding on interest to non-resident lenders is 5% for corporate lenders unless a treaty reduces it further (often already at or below the 5% or 10% rate). This Article requires the LLC to withhold from payments to offshore parent financing entities and license holders.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP, a taxpayer must prepare and maintain Local File and Master File if: (1) related-party transaction revenue exceeds VND 30 billion per annum; or (2) total revenue from all activities exceeds VND 50 billion; or (3) total assets exceed VND 100 billion; or (4) the taxpayer is a related party in a group with ultimate parent revenue exceeding VND 100 billion (for Master File). The Country-by-Country Report is required if the ultimate parent group's consolidated global revenue is VND 20 trillion or more. Even if below thresholds, the taxpayer must still complete the related-party transaction declaration in the CIT finalization return, and the tax authority may adjust prices.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam applies anti-abuse and economic substance principles primarily through the Law on Tax Administration No. 38/2019/QH14 (Article 7) and Decree 132/2020/ND-CP (GAAR). For foreign-invested enterprises, documentation must prove that the Vietnamese LLC has real business substance, including employees, premises, business records, and actual performance of the offshore securities brokerage activity. The Vietnamese LLC cannot be used as a shell booking entity. The State Securities Commission must issue a securities brokerage license, and the entity must meet capital and operational substance requirements under the Law on Securities 2019. A letter-box entity without substance in Vietnam will have its income adjusted to a deemed taxable amount, and its transfer pricing documentation will be disregarded.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating revenue from securities brokerage commissions; invoicing for fictitious transactions; maintaining undisclosed offshore trading accounts; misreporting income to shift profits offshore; failure to register certain revenue streams.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law on Tax Administration 38/2019/QH14 and Penal Code 100/2015/QH13 (as amended), tax evasion is punishable by a fine of 1.5 to 3 times the evaded tax amount, plus late interest. Criminal liability: imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine up to VND 1 billion for evading tax of VND 100 million or more; up to 7 years for larger amounts; prohibited from holding certain offices for 1–3 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives, directors, and managers who knowingly order or approve false returns are personally liable. Courts may impose travel bans, passport revocation, and restriction on leaving Viet Nam. Directors face criminal imprisonment under Article 200 of the Penal Code. Civil restitution to the state from personal assets is enforced if the corporate entity lacks funds (piercing the corporate veil).

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC is operated as a shell or letter-box company with no real offices, no operational personnel, no brokerage license in Viet Nam, or without actual client-facing or order-execution substance; transactions are booked offshore to exploit treaty or tax advantages.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax authorities may apply general anti-avoidance under Decree 132/2020 by disregarding the entity or transaction, re-characterizing income, imposing deemed profits, and charging additional CIT at 20% plus late interest and penalties. The relevant entity may lose access to tax incentives. The securities license can be revoked by the State Securities Commission. Criminal liability for fraud under Article 174 may arise if used to defraud investors or tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for restitution of taxes evaded, monetary penalties up to VND 1 billion, and imprisonment under tax evasion or fraud charges. Travel bans and asset freezes are used to secure collection; Taiwanese-style shell splits are not tolerated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately overstating losses arising from offshore transactions, manipulation of inventory, artificial year-end accruals, or acquiring loss-making entities solely to absorb disappearing profits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority re-adjusts taxable income and rejects the loss carryforward. Penalties under Article 14 of Decree 125/2020 for tax return inaccuracies: up to VND 20 million if no underpayment, or up to VND 50 million for serious errors; if underpayment arises, penalty 20% of unpaid tax plus late interest at 0.03% per day and criminal prosecution for evasion if intentional.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approve fabricated loss schedules are jointly liable for underpaid CIT, interest, and penalties. Fraudulent tax loss certification is a criminal act subject to travel bans and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Non-Compliance / Unjustified Offshore Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the related party transaction declaration, failing to maintain contemporaneous TP documentation (Local File / Master File / CbCR), applying non-arm's length commission allocations, charging excessive management or support fees from offshore, or using unbenchmarked intercompany loans with excessive interest rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Decree 132/2020 and Law on Tax Administration, tax authority may reassess profits and impose additional CIT with a penalty of up to 20% of underpaid tax plus late interest (0.03%/day). Refusal to provide documentation shifts the burden of proof; tax authority may apply deemed pricing. Administrative fines up to VND 75 million can be imposed under Decree 125. Under repeated or aggravated circumstances, criminal tax evasion liability applies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and finance officers who approve non-arm’s length cross-border payments are personally exposed for tax collection deficiencies. In egregious cases, travel bans, bank account freezes, and direct garnishment of personal assets. Criminal prosecution under Article 202 of the Penal Code (violation of tax regulations) may be pursued.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Foreign Contractor Withholding Tax (FCT) Remittance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC pays royalties, interest, technical service fees, or brokerage commissions to offshore personnel, software providers, or affiliates without withholding the applicable FCT (currently 5% CIT on interest, 10% CIT on royalties, and 0-5% VAT; or 10% CIT for services) within 20 days from the time the liability arises or before foreign bank remittance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: If not withheld/remitted, the LLC is liable for the unpaid FCT amount, plus late interest, and is denied deduction for such expenses. Administrative fines equal 100% of unpaid withholding taxes if disclosed too late, or up to 2-4 times if concealed. Criminal tax evasion penalties may apply where the failure is deliberate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general managers who knowingly disburse foreign payments without FCT withholding are personally liable for the underpaid tax. Travel restrictions are routinely used to compel payment; imprisonment up to 7 years for deliberate evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The LLC does not implement customer due diligence (CDD) under the Law on Anti-Money Laundering 2022, fails to report suspicious transactions to the State Bank's Anti-Money Laundering Department (TPL), or handles transactions for shell clients or unknown beneficial owners; operating without effective compliance in high-risk offshore brokerage.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Decree on AML administrative sanctions, fines can reach VND 2 billion for serious violations; repeat violations can require suspension of operations or revocation of license. For criminal money laundering (Article 251 Penal Code), imprisonment up to 15 years, significant corporate fines, and asset confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers can be personally fined (VND 100-500 million), imprisoned, or subject to travel bans and professional bans. Inadequate AML oversight is sufficient for personal prosecution; the corporate veil does not protect gross negligent directors.
